CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing and chest pain with swallowing for several weeks.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports difficulty swallowing for the past several weeks, particularly with larger pieces of food that feel stuck. He describes pain with swallowing located in the chest, occurring most of the time but not with every swallow. Pain is worse with bigger pieces of food. Patient reports recent stress related to relocation from west coast to east coast over the last couple of months, during which time he has been eating poorly, consuming foods like pizza and burgers, and reports weight gain. Denies weight loss from symptoms. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools. Reports occasional abdominal pain in the epigastric area.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nausea or vomiting. Denies diarrhea. Reports occasional epigastric abdominal pain. Denies fever. Denies rash, lesions, or bruising.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast. Reports significant stress related to move. Considering driving cross-country with pet dog. Has been eating unhealthy foods (pizza, burgers) due to stress and busy schedule. Unclear alcohol and caffeine use history discussed during visit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 133/70, heart rate normal, no fever, respiratory rate 19, oxygen saturation 100%.
General: Recent weight gain of approximately 10 pounds over the last month noted in chart.
HEENT: No ulcers or thrush. Tonsils midline.
Neck: No adenopathy. No thyromegaly.
Abdomen: Nondistended, active bowel sounds, pain to palpation of epigastric area, negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: No rash, lesions, or bruising.
Eyes: Equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow showed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis.
Plan: Prescribe Protonix 40 mg once daily, take first thing in the morning. Prescribe Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat esophageal and gastric lining. Schedule upper endoscopy. Dietary modifications: decrease alcohol and caffeine, avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve, eat slowly and chew food thoroughly. Follow-up appointment next week for upper endoscopy.
